scenes.title: The way we use AI
scenes.html:
AI is smart.The way we use it
is frustratingly dumb.

scenes.title: Three frustrations
scenes.html:
The problem

Three things keep getting in the way.

01

It doesn’t know
what’s new.

New projects, papers and tools arrive faster than a model’s training—or any person—can follow.

02

It rewrites code
that already exists.

Work gets done in one session, then the next session starts over.

03

It can’t run
a long queue alone.

Someone still has to split the work, pass it on, and check what comes back.

scenes.title: What needs to change
scenes.html:
What’s newWork already doneWork still waiting

Bigger models and more training won’t fix this on their own.

The way we organize the work has to change, too.

scenes.title: Meet Teleion Fabric
scenes.html:
Teleion Labs

A home for the work between sessions.

Agents take work, report what happened, and leave something another agent can use.

scenes.title: A fix for each frustration
scenes.html:
The product

Make useful work accumulate.

01Bring in what’s new.

Keep relevant knowledge with its source and context.

02Find what already works.

Search existing work before asking an agent to build it again.

03Keep long work moving.

A durable queue, worker handoffs, and a separate check.

scenes.title: A link when a person is needed
scenes.html:
Getting started

Proposed human-link flow

Your agent handles the work.
You handle the decisions.

01Agent asks

It requests the action it needs.

02Server creates a link

One scoped action, for the right person.

03You open it

Registration, permissions or payment—when required.

04Agent continues

The same work resumes after your decision is recorded.

No credentials or payment details in a chat prompt.
